articles.title: Walter Koenig on the Lean Years After Star Trek: TOS – ‘The Phone Didn't Ring’
articles.summary: Star Trek legend Walter Koenig looks back on the good, the bad, and the hilarious after 57 years of the franchise.
articles.body:
With the sad news that Star Trek legend Walter Koenig has died at the age of 90 , it seemed like folks might be interested in taking a look at this interview that I did with the Chekov actor a couple of years back while onboard the annual Star Trek cruise. Koenig was very forthcoming with me about his Trek tenure, which of course defined his career in the popular eye, but also represented its share of challenges, like in the difficult years after The Original Series went off the air and work dried up for him... until the franchise was revived on the big screen.

Read on for that chat as it was originally published back in 2024... And rest in peace, Walter Koenig.

It’s the last day of the Star Trek cruise – officially known as Star Trek: The Cruise VII – and it’s down to the wire. After trying to land an interview with Trek legend Walter Koenig for the past week, I’ve just been told by a rep to call the actor’s cabin directly. Me? Call Chekov?! Bozhe moi!

Koenig of course played Pavel Chekov in the original Star Trek television series as well as seven of the movies. And while the cruise ship has been full of Star Trek actors, getting to talk to Koenig, an OG of the franchise, is an opportunity I just can’t let pass by. So I call the number, finding the unmistakable (if not Russian-accented) voice of the actor at the other end of the line. “Come on up to my cabin and we’ll talk” is his simple response. You could practically hear the ship standing down from Red Alert at that moment.

It turns out Walter Koenig isn’t just a nice guy, but the 87-year-old actor is also very open about his experiences as part of the Star Trek phenomenon for the past 57 years – from the highs to the lows, the satisfaction of being part of such a beloved series, but also the frustrations that have peppered the experience at times.

I had attended a panel that Koenig put on earlier in the cruise where he spent an hour taking questions from the fans. It was surprising how forgiving he was of the slights, perceived or otherwise, that some of his castmates lodged at series star William Shatner over the years. Koenig explains that in the 1960s, there was a different sense about participation in television and how big an actor’s role should or should not be.

“We really were operating under a caste system … where you had the stars, and then you had supporting actors,” he said. “And it was just an unspoken sense that the stars, the two or three people who drove the stories, and who [had] 80% of the screen time. Those were the people that you acknowledged first and foremost. The supporting actors, depending on the series but certainly in general, were just… it was sort of self-explanatory that we would be there to support them. We were there as the expositional characters, the ones who helped push the story, but not really given the opportunity to probe who they were as characters. That wasn't as important as it was to get to know the stars.”

That meant that Shatner, Leonard Nimoy, and DeForest Kelley got most of the screen time on The Original Series, even if, as Koenig acknowledges, Chekov and his fellow supporting players got something juicy “once in a while.” Who can forget Chekov’s misplaced claims that Russia invented… everything, after all?

“[They] got most of the screen time, got most of the attention, and we accepted it,” he continued. “That's the way things went. And I think Bill [Shatner] had grown up with that sense, and his popularity was so immense, and he was an extremely talented fellow. And so he, I think, just unconsciously accepted the way things were. […] So there was less recognition for us. During the years we were shooting, I never felt left behind because I never anticipated more than that. I felt very lucky that I had been cast in a situation where I would get a check every week. It was quite amazing to me. […] It was only when we started doing the fan-driven conventions that we began to suspect that the fans really, really enjoyed our participation.”

Koenig remembers when he got the Star Trek job. The show had been on the air for a year already, and while he says “I'm sure there are people who would love to hear me wax philosophical about Star Trek,” he adds that “the first thing for me was that it was a steady job.”

He was playing a character who was younger than he was, and in fact he had already been married for two years. He and his wife’s first child was born in 1968 while he was shooting the show. So for Koenig, his first thought was that he had a family to support.

“I didn't understand how profound it was in terms of the way people related to it and the humanity that was part of this show,” he said. “It was a perspective that we embraced […] Gene Roddenberry created the show to talk about how people could be better than they were and how we could live in a future which was better than what we were experiencing at the time. But mostly, I was just pleased to be working.”

Koenig acknowledges the difficulties that he faced after The Original Series went off the air in 1969. By the early 1970s, finding work as an actor had become difficult for him. And it’s not like he was making big bucks when he was the navigator of the starship Enterprise.

“Everybody thinks if you're an actor, and certainly if you're an actor and on a television series, you must be doing very well,” Koenig said. “Well, I was barely making more than minimum the first season. The second season I was on the show … I had a contract. I was paid a week's wage whether I worked a day or a week. So I made a little bit more. Whereas I made $10,000 for the whole year in 1967, I made $11,000 in 1968. Well, that'll only go so far.”

Of course, the idea of the Star Trek movies that would eventually come was a mere glimmer in Gene Roddenberry’s eye at that point, and Koenig had a wife and a baby son that he had to support.

“And the phone didn't ring,” he recalled. “I just didn't have any opportunities. I think I had a few years where I was doing guest-starring roles, and as I look back at it, as I have over the years, and wondered why it stopped happening ... Well, it happened because I looked younger than I was, which meant that I could play teenagers and they wouldn't have to hire a teacher [on set]. That was number one. And having that opportunity, I got to make some fairly significant contributions as a guest actor. So the time came I turned 30. I still looked young, but not compared to somebody who was really 18 or under. And so the work slowed down significantly. In fact, the year before Star Trek, I had a very tough time getting any roles. Star Trek in 1967 just resurrected my career and became the principal source of revenue and popularity and creativity for me.”

The first movie in the franchise, Star Trek: The Motion Picture, would revive Chekov and his crewmembers in 1979. But prior to that, there were several attempts to bring back Star Trek as a TV series. Koenig recalls that the studio was in touch with him on two or possibly three occasions for these runs at resurrecting the USS Enterprise, but the first attempt he was actually not meant to be a part of.

“We were coming back about six or seven years after we had been canceled,” he said. “I was already 11 years older than the character was supposed to be. And the sense was that I couldn't pull it off. That's what they said. So I was not approached because I'd have to have been 17 or 18 years younger than I actually was. The truth is it was disappointing. It was very disappointing. On the other hand, I've always lived with the sense that if it can go wrong, it will. There's always been that very skeptical, cynical sense that I've lived with, so that when things go right, I'm always surprised. It's always fresh.”

Eventually Koenig was called back for a different planned TV revival, and he laughs about how he was the only one who still fit his costume. But the laughs didn’t last.

“An hour [later at] home, the phone rang, ‘Oh, we're not going forward,’” he recalled. “And that happened a second time. And so you get gun-shy and you get the sense that it ain't never going to happen.”

As the 1970s progressed the Star Trek convention scene grew, and it began to be not only a source of income for Koenig and his fellow actors, but also a place where the true impact of Chekov and the other supporting characters became clear to the actors.

“When we started doing conventions and received the kind of a approbation that we did, that's part of the actor psyche,” he said. “We all loved to be stroked and these fans were so generous in that regard. […] People are still recognizing me and saying nice things. And now I've long since embraced the political ramifications, the social ramifications of what Star Trek stands for. I'm in accord with that, very vociferously.”

Of course, it did happen eventually with the aforementioned The Motion Picture, but Koenig couldn’t quite believe it even after they were on stage shooting the first day.

“The first shot was a panning shot of the bridge, and everybody at their stations, and I had not yet accepted the idea that we were really making this film,” he laughed. “The second shot was Captain Kirk steps out of the lift [and] Uhura, Sulu, and Chekov run up to him. And as they were lighting that, and we were standing there waiting to shoot it with Bill there and Nichelle [Nichols] and George [Takei] and I, I said, ‘Holy cow, we're making this movie. We are really making this movie.’ And that's when I started believing.”

It’s a question the guy has been asked a million times before, but I couldn’t help but ask him for the millionth and one time: What is his favorite Chekov moment?

“It was not that significant, but it was just such a delight,” Koenig responded. “And that was the improvisation that I did in Star Trek IV [The Voyage Home] when I approached the crowd and asked them where the ‘nuclear wessels’ were. That was just great fun. I loved the opportunity to do comedy anyway, and that was a delightful little moment. It was a moment. It was not more than a moment. But when Leonard [Nimoy, who directed the film] finally yelled, ‘Cut,’ and I looked at his big, broad smile on his face, I felt really good. And I thought that this was great fun.”

It's certainly one of those iconic moments from Star Trek and one that even non-Trekkies might recall. As Chekov and Uhura, who have time-travelled to the 20th century with the rest of their crew, look for a naval base with, ahem, nuclear vessels , they innocently ask people for directions on the streets of San Francisco.

“They were all extras except for one,” Koenig said of the bystanders in the scene. “One young woman came by with her dog ... She wasn't supposed to get into the scene, but she walked into the scene, and she was one of the people that I saw, and I didn't know that she was not part of our group. So I asked her the question, and she started telling me where Alameda was, and they kept it. They kept it. I made sure. When they finally said, ‘Cut,’ the first thing I did was I went to the, I think it was the assistant director, and said, ‘Get her information. Make sure we have her so we can use this footage if indeed it works out in the film.’ And the hysterical irony is that she wasn't an actress. She ended up signing autographs at conventions!”

articles.title: Epic Games Boss Tim Sweeney Doubles Down on Valve Criticism, Says Steam's AI Content Disclosure Is a 'Political Act'
articles.summary: Epic Games boss Tim Sweeney spent the weekend doubling down on his severe criticism of Valve, calling Steam’s AI content disclosure a “political act.”
articles.body:
Epic Games boss Tim Sweeney spent the weekend doubling down on his severe criticism of Valve, calling Steam’s AI content disclosure a “political act.”

The controversial majority owner of Epic is all in on AI, having recently triggered a “huge pivot” of the company to retool it for “maximum AI acceleration,” Sweeney said . Epic is a long-standing rival of Gabe Newell’s Valve, with the Epic Games Store struggling to make a dent in Steam’s dominance over the PC gaming market even as it offers developers more financially beneficial terms.

Sweeney is particularly upset with Steam’s AI content disclosure policy, which requires developers to disclose the use of AI in “creating content that ships with your game, and is consumed by players.” This includes content such as artwork, sound, narrative, and localization. It does not include “efficiency gains” through the use of AI tools.

On Friday, Sweeney hit out at Valve’s policy , saying “forcing developers to write a political statement to be used against them by the hate mob they’re helping organize is abhorrent.” This statement sparked a backlash online, with a number of people — developers included — confused by the suggestion that an AI disclosure was political in any way, and insisting that Valve was only providing clarity its customers wanted.

“Customers have a right to know what they’re buying,” David Goldfarb, founder of Metal Hellsinger developer The Outsiders and former Battlefield developer, replied. “They still bought Arc Raiders, they will definitely buy games they want to buy, AI use or no. Does it disadvantage small teams who need to leverage AI to survive? Jury’s out. Calling it a hate mob is far-fetched.”

Undeterred, Sweeney issued a number of social media posts defending his position, saying AI disclosures are “just as partisan as mandatory political essays or forcing developers to list their voting history to drive cancel campaigns and public struggle sessions.”

When one person challenged Sweeney on this, accusing him of being "anti-consumer" for forcing something consumers don't like on them, the Fortnite boss compared Steam's AI disclosures to Valve forcing developers to list their political affiliations.

"Say there is a large contingent of gamers that don’t like democrats or, equivalently, republicans. Should Valve force developers to list their political affiliation? Is that pro-consumer? Do you think that policy would have a positive effect on gaming?" he said . As you can imagine, this statement was ridiculed in the replies, with one person saying "equating AI to how a person votes is pure cope gymnastics."

Again, undeterred, Sweeney claimed that Valve is hitting developer revenue by “undermining their business with these AI hate campaigns,” insisting on “a real economic cost to Valve’s foray into forced political disclosures.”

He continued : “a substantial number of users would love to have mandatory political opinion disclosures for developers, with several saying they take it upon themselves to surface this info in reviews since it’s not disclosed on product pages.

“The primary use of both categories of disclosures is to drive cancel campaigns against games and deprive them of revenue and livelihood unless they get onboard with the movement’s political goals. Yes, blocking free choice to adopt productive technology is a political act.”

Earlier this month, Epic revealed a newly refreshed version of the Epic Games Launcher , its Steam-like platform that provides access to the Epic Games Store, your games library, social features, and a developer’s hub. And, in keeping with the company’s push for AI-assisted development , this new version of the launcher was created using generative artificial intelligence. “Programming is hard,” wrote Epic in a new blog post . “So, instead of doing that, we vibe coded a new Epic Games Launcher that’s way faster and more responsive than the current one, and has a new look.”

Epic then launched an Unreal Engine vibe coding contest with an image of a six-fingered hand, presumably as a joke about poor quality AI images.

Vibe your way to 50K. The 2026 Epic AI MegaJam begins Nov 12: — Unreal Engine (@UnrealEngine) October 22, 2026

Vibe your way to 50K. The 2026 Epic AI MegaJam begins Nov 12:

Through it all, Valve has done what it does best: remain quiet. The long-running joke that Gabe Newell simply sits back and waits for his competitors to make mistakes seems particularly relevant here, as Tim Sweeney continues to tweet his outrage over Valve and Steam. Meanwhile, earlier this month Steam broke its all-time record for concurrent users yet again, with 43.5 million people logged in at the same time.

Photographer: SeongJoon Cho/Bloomberg via Getty Images

articles.title: GTA 6 tampoco se perdió el Clásico: El Camp Nou, otra pieza clave en la estrategia de Rockstar Games
articles.standfirst: El videojuego estuvo presente en la victoria del Real Madrid ante el FC Barcelona
articles.summary: El videojuego estuvo presente en la victoria del Real Madrid ante el FC Barcelona
articles.body: Ayer vivimos uno de los momentos clave de la temporada futbolera y deportiva en general y es que un nuevo Clásico llegaba a nuestras vidas. FC Barcelona y Real Madrid se volvían a ver las caras en un duelo en el que los de Hansi Flick llegaban como claros favoritos, por las sensaciones de inicio de temporada y por ser locales. Pero el Real Madrid sorprendió a todos en el Camp Nou sacando una muy meritoria victoria en un momento en el que pocos confiaban en los de Mourinho. Más allá de lo meramente futbolístico, todos sabemos lo que genera un partido de esta magnitud. Millones de personas en todo el mundo están pendientes de lo que ocurre durante esos 90 minutos. Pues bien, Rockstar Games también es plenamente consciente de la expectación que genera un Clásico y por eso convirtió este acontecimiento en una pieza más de su estrategia. Y es que durante las últimas semanas estamos viendo cómo la compañía está llevado a cabo una estrategia de marketing para promocionar el GTA 6 que va más allá de la publicidad en web, redes sociales o las típicas plataformas, ya que está llegando a las ciudades más importantes del mundo para dejar su huella. Más que conocido es todo el movimiento que está generando Rockstar en Miami, ciudad en la que está basado el GTA 6, donde los coches del videojuego están llegando a las calles y la ciudad en general se está transformando en el juego. Además, por ejemplo, hemos visto un cartel gigante en París con la imagen del juego, pero esto no acaba aquí. El Clásico también se convirtió en uno de esos puntos claves de Rockstar para promocionar la salida del GTA 6 el próximo 19 de noviembre. Y es que durante el encuentro vimos la publicidad del videojuego en los carteles de pie de campo, dejando una imagen que pasará a la historia y que confirma que Rockstar está llevando su estrategia a otro nivel, 'conquistando' los lugares más importantes en el momento preciso.

articles.title: Red weather warning issued for Isle of Man coastal overtopping
articles.summary: The rare red weather warning for waves crashing onto coastal roads means extreme conditions with a risk to life.
articles.body:
A red weather warning has been issued for the Isle of Man for large waves crashing onto coastal roads.

It is in place for coastal overtopping from 22:00 until 01:00 GMT on Tuesday.

A red warning is rare and means extreme conditions are likely, with a risk to life, as well as possible widespread damage, travel disruption and interruptions to power and communications.

The government has asked people to take the "warning seriously and avoid affected coastal areas."

Coastal overtopping or wave overtopping is the amount of water that is discharged by waves over a structure such as a breakwater.

When the waves break, it causes water to flow onto the land with debris.

Alongside the red warning, an amber one for inner harbor flooding has been issued by forecasters at Ronaldsway Met Office.

"Inner harbour flooding expected around the time of the high tide tonight, with a storm surge in the Irish Sea," it said.

The banks of River Sulby to Gardener's Lane.

The Met Office said flood defences should also be deployed for the lowest-lying parts of Castletown Harbour.

In addition, a yellow warning for severe gales will come into force from 18:00 until 06:00 on Tuesday.

Gusts between 50-60 mph (80-96 km/h) are expected widely with up to 65mph (104 km/h) forecast for higher ground exposed coastal areas.

"This may result in fallen branches/ trees and disruption to travel," forecasters said.

The Liverpool crossing, which was scheduled for 15:00, left Douglas Harbour earlier at 06:00.

While both Manannan Larne sailings were cancelled.

At Ronaldsway Airport, all scheduled flights are going ahead as planned however, the airport have asked for passengers to arrive two hours early due to the number of disrupted flights taking off today.

Over the weekend, Storm Boelo kept teams from the Department of Infrastrucutre busy.

The DOI said crews dealt with 85 fallen trees, 31 flooding incidents, and more than 25 other storm-related call-outs.

Sailings and flights to and from the island were also cancelled.

articles.title: EA Sports FC 27 dicta sentencia: este será el ganador del Balón de Oro 2026
articles.standfirst: Este será el futbolista que se lleve el galardón según el popular videojuego
articles.summary: Este será el futbolista que se lleve el galardón según el popular videojuego
articles.body: Ha llegado uno de los momentos más esperados del año en el mundo del fútbol: conocer quién será el próximo ganador del Balón de Oro. Con varios candidatos que han firmado una temporada sobresaliente, la batalla por hacerse con el prestigioso galardón promete estar más igualada que nunca. A priori, los tres grandes favoritos para levantar el Balón de Oro 2026 son Lamine Yamal, Harry Kane y Kylian Mbappé. Los tres futbolistas han protagonizado una campaña en la que han demostrado su enorme calidad y capacidad para marcar diferencias sobre el terreno de juego. Sin embargo, ¿quién se llevará finalmente el premio? Desde MARCA Gaming hemos querido resolver esta incógnita de una manera muy especial. Para ello, hemos simulado el Modo Carrera de EA Sports FC 27 hasta conocer al ganador del Balón de Oro. Y, aunque esperábamos que la decisión estuviera entre los tres grandes candidatos, el videojuego ya ha dictado sentencia y ha elegido a su propio favorito. Con EA Sports FC 27 ya disponible, desde MARCA Gaming hemos aprovechado la ocasión para comprobar qué futbolista termina imponiéndose en la carrera por el Balón de Oro según el nuevo videojuego de fútbol de Electronic Arts. Para descubrirlo, hemos recurrido al Modo Carrera y hemos avanzado en la simulación hasta conocer el nombre del jugador que consigue hacerse con el galardón en esta edición. Una prueba que nos permite comprobar cómo interpreta el título la evolución de las grandes estrellas del fútbol mundial y quién termina ocupando el primer puesto entre los mejores jugadores del planeta. Y el elegido por EA Sports FC 27 no es otro que Lamine Yamal. El joven futbolista del FC Barcelona se impone en la simulación y se convierte en el ganador del Balón de Oro 2026 según el videojuego. Una elección que, sin duda, le sitúa como uno de los grandes protagonistas de esta particular predicción virtual. El resultado no resulta del todo descabellado. Lamine Yamal se ha consolidado como una de las grandes figuras del fútbol mundial y su talento le permite competir de tú a tú con jugadores de la talla de Harry Kane y Kylian Mbappé. Su capacidad para desequilibrar partidos, generar ocasiones y convertirse en un futbolista decisivo le ha colocado entre los nombres más destacados de la actualidad. Eso sí, que FC 27 haya elegido a Lamine Yamal no significa que el español vaya a ganar necesariamente el Balón de Oro en la realidad. La simulación del videojuego es simplemente una predicción virtual y no tiene por qué coincidir con la decisión final de los votantes.

It will be released in 2027 for PC.
articles.body:
If you've ever wondered what a fusion of Vampire Survivors and Heroes of Might and Magic would look like, then Heroes Never Die might be the game for you. It's a newly announced fantasy strategy game from developer Ludogram that "aims to take the best of the survival formula and fuse it with more tactical decisions, real-time army building, and powerful fantasy heroes." It will be released in 2027 for PC.

In Heroes Never Die, you'll choose your titular hero – there are over 20 in the lineup – and battle not just monster hordes but also rival heroes. Each hero has their own skills, but no matter who you pick, you'll seek to upgrade your town by gathering resources and fighting foes. There are also four factions and over 60 different units, with the developers promising that no two runs will be alike.

“We’re delighted to finally announce Heroes Never Die, a project we’ve been working on in the shadows for a couple of years”, said creative director Edouard Gaudel. “We cannot wait to see our first players fighting hordes of monsters, and evolving their armies while meeting our heroes. Don’t forget to join our upcoming Playtest!”

If you're interested, you can sign up for the private playtest and/or wishlist Heroes Never Die on Steam .

articles.title: PlayStation Handheld May Have Exclusive Next-Gen AMD Graphics, Report Suggests
articles.summary: Sony may have exclusive access to AMD's next-generation graphics architecture for a potential PlayStation handheld, the tech experts at Digital Foundry have said.
articles.body:
Sony may have exclusive access to AMD's next-generation graphics architecture for a potential PlayStation handheld, the tech experts at Digital Foundry have said.

There have been rumors of a next-generation PlayStation handheld for some time now, after the success of the Nintendo Switch and a wide gamut of PC gaming handhelds . Indeed, in June, Sony Interactive Entertainment CEO Hideaki Nishino suggested PlayStation may move towards more hybrid, Switch-like consoles in the future to match modern on-the-go players.

When I watched the latest Patreon-exclusive DF Direct , Digital Foundry's Richard Leadbetter claimed that "there's been some behind-the-scenes discussion that Sony has an exclusive of sorts with AMD for RDNA 5 for handheld," and that the only other, presumably handheld, chip he knows of in production at AMD is what's going to be known as Z3, which is unlikely to have RDNA 5 graphics.

The 100 Best PlayStation Games of All Time

AMD and Sony have been working closely for the last couple of years, teaming up on an initiative called 'Project Amethyst,' which ultimately resulted in both PSSR 2 on the PS5 Pro and FSR 4.1 for PC and Xbox.

Speaking of Xbox, it sounds like Microsoft has handheld gaming plans of its own. Project Helix will include a whole range of devices , we were recently told, and a handheld will reportedly be the first out the gate. Fortune recently reported that Microsoft plans to release a handheld by holiday 2027, with the next-gen console following in 2028. The chips going into either of these platforms hasn't been confirmed, but AMD did come out and tease that FSR Diamond would be launching with Project Helix – of which the handheld is a part of – and that would likely be running on RDNA 5.

AMD would have reason to supercharge its handheld chip offerings for a wide range of devices, as well. Intel's Panther Lake handheld chip launched at Computex 2026 and, at least in my testing, absolutely bodies the AMD Ryzen Z2 Extreme . The Z2 Extreme only uses an RDNA 3.5 GPU, which was already an older architecture when it launched last year. The Intel Arc G3, on the other hand, uses the same GPU that powers its latest laptops, just with a few of the CPU cores disabled.

With how expensive handhelds have become lately, the whole category is in danger of vanishing until the RAM crisis abates , and so it's possible that Sony's handheld is the only one that springs for the added cost of RDNA 5. But, unless Sony inks some kind of exclusive deal with AMD, I am sure other devices using RDNA 5 will exist eventually – maybe even Xbox's own first-party handheld.

This isn’t the first PlayStation handheld tease, either. Last year, Moore’s Law Is Dead reported on an unannounced PS6 handheld that would be dockable and backwards compatible with PS4 and PS5 games. There was also a brief mention of what was described as a PS6 S, which sounded like it could be to the PS6 what the Xbox Series S is to the Xbox Series X. If true, you’d assume it would be a cheaper option.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: The Sony WH-1000XM4C bring back a beloved headphone design
articles.summary: They’re based on six-year-old technology, but the XM4C still deliver respectable performance, and I love using them.
articles.body: When Sony announced the WH-1000XM4C headphones, I was perplexed. A product revamp usually includes at least one or two significant improvements. Or if it’s a nostalgia play, it’s from a decades-old product and not one that came out in 2020. Beyond a few minor tweaks, though, the XM4C are remarkably similar to their six-year-old namesake, the beloved WH-1000XM4. They even use the same processor for active noise cancellation (ANC). And while I went into this review questioning the XM4C’s existence, after spending some time with them, I get it. The Sony XM4C aren’t the cutting edge of headphone technology, but they are great headphones that I love using. They still sound great, the design is classic, and they get you pretty close to the performance of Sony’s current-gen flagship, the WH-1000XM6, for a lot less money. [Product: Sony WH-1000XM4C headphones | What I, and many others, loved about the original XM4 is still at the heart of the XM4C. They fold up into a compact size and come with a hard-shell zippered case (which now has its loop on the zipper instead of the edge) that’s easy for travel. The faux-leather ear cups are squishy and comfortable — I wore them for hours at a time during testing without issue. Codec support is also the same as the XM4, with SBC, AAC, and LDAC for high-res wireless audio with supported devices. The similarities continue with the XM4C’s 40mm driver and, by extension, their sound. Bass is on the heavier side as it is with the XM4, but it isn’t overpowering and instead supports everything above it. Kick drum and tom hits have good oomph and definition. Low-end loving tracks like “bad guy” by Billie Eilish really drive forward. The midrange — like the attack of the acoustic guitar in Tracy Chapman’s “Fast Car” or the bite of Robert Plant’s vocals — can sound slightly covered or muted. It’s not something I hear on my original XM4s, although the difference isn’t drastic. There’s a 10-band EQ in the Sony Sound Connect app (up from five bands on the original XM4) and after boosting the frequencies between 1kHz and 4kHz, the midrange opened up. But even without that small EQ change, the XM4C sound great. In a world that’s continuing to move away from 3.5mm connections, the XM4C still have one, which works in both powered mode (to use the ANC) or with the headphones off if the battery is low. Like the XM4 (and the XM5 and even last year’s XM6), the XM4C only support wired listening over 3.5mm, though, and not USB-C. The XM4C headphones also only include a 3.5mm cable. You’ll need to provide your own USB-C cable for charging. [Image: The XM4C (in white) are remarkably similar to the original XM4 (in black), and that’s not a bad thing. As with the XM4, the XM4C use four mics with Sony’s older QN1 chip for noise canceling, and because of that the ANC performance is basically the same. Going back and forth between the two, the XM4C blocks out a little more of the low end from air conditioners and big trucks driving by outside. But that difference could come from the XM4C’s ear pads, which are six years newer than the worn ones on my XM4. Not that the XM4C’s ANC is bad, but it’s where their six-year-old tech shows the most. ANC has improved a lot over the past few years, and there are headphones that offer comparable performance for half the price, like the Anker Soundcore Space 2. And it doesn’t compare to the more expensive headphones in Sony’s XM series. Both the XM5 (which also has the QN1 chip, although with eight mics) and XM6 (12 total mics with the more advanced QN3) are better at isolation across the frequency range, especially at the lower end. The slightly more expensive second-generation Bose QuietComfort Headphones block lower frequencies a bit better than the XM4C, too. Still, the performance is solid, and I never felt distracted by outside noise when it was active. [Image: While recent headphones have been eschewing the 3.5mm jack, the XM4C include one for wired listening. It’s the same with call quality. The XM4C block ambient sound on calls well, and my voice is clear and understandable, but sometimes louder noises break through or cause my voice to sound a bit compressed. They get the job done; they’re just not top tier like the XM6 (which cost $160 more). One of the selling points of the XM4C is their replaceable battery — required by upcoming EU regulations for Sony to sell them in Europe. The replacement battery is not for sale in North America, and there’s no indication from Sony when (or if) it might be available here. At the moment, there also aren’t any instructions on how to do the replacement yourself. The ear cups are definitely easier to remove than before — I was able to pop them off and on with my hands instead of prying them up with an extra tool. But once they’re off, there’s no easy way to figure out which screws to remove to get to the battery. (Removing just the four visibly obvious silver screws with arrows pointing to them doesn’t do it.) Now, this isn’t a huge deal on brand-new headphones with batteries that should last you a few years, but it’s also not encouraging for American customers expecting the extra longevity that a user-replaceable battery provides. The change to a removable battery has also slightly affected battery life on the XM4C, down to 27 hours with ANC on from the 30 hours with the XM4. It’s still more than enough to get through a few days, though. One disappointing omission is Bluetooth LE, and therefore Auracast support. With the move to Bluetooth 6.0, and the fact the XM5 and XM6 both support it, I was hoping these would, too. It doesn’t mean they might not eventually get Auracast through a firmware update. (That’s what happened with the XM5.) It’s just a shame they don’t have it at release. [Image: The XM4C can fold into a compact size. The XM4C also keep the capacitive touch controls apart from the power and ANC buttons, like in the XM series. A sensor on the right ear cup allows for track and volume controls. Holding your palm over it activates transparency mode until you move it away for quick moments when you need to hear someone. The controls work decently, but I’ve always preferred physical buttons. The release of the XM4C was a surprise, but it’s a welcome one. Even with only minor improvements on a six-year-old design, the XM4C are still great headphones. I enjoy how they sound, the ANC works well, and they’re incredibly comfortable. Is $300 a bit more than I’d expect for headphones based on a model from 2020? Yeah, a little. But those looking for an XM4 replacement will be incredibly happy with them. The Sony XM4C prove that even though a design is old, it doesn’t mean it should be forgotten. Photography by John Higgins / The Verge

articles.title: Walter Koenig, Star Trek's Chekov, Dies at Age 90
articles.summary: Walter Koenig, who played Chekov on the original Star Trek series, has died at age 90. Koenig joined the NBC series Star Trek in its second season as Russian crewmember Ensign Pavel Andreievich Chekov.
articles.body:
Walter Koenig, who played Chekov on the original Star Trek series, has died at age 90.

“The late actor's rep tells us ... Walter's daughter, Danielle, and his niece were by his side when he died of old age at his home in North Hollywood on Sunday,” TMZ reports .

Koenig joined the NBC series Star Trek in its second season as the USS Enterprise’s Russian crewmember Ensign Pavel Andreievich Chekov. With his Beatles-style mop of hair, the boyish Chekov was meant to appeal to younger viewers a la Davy Jones of The Monkees.

As Chekov, Koenig would appear in the latter two seasons of the original series and then in all six feature films featuring the cast.

With Koenig’s death, only William Shatner (Captain Kirk) and George Takei (Mr. Sulu) remain alive from the original cast.

Takei took to social media to salute his longtime co-star:

Marvin Walter Koenig was born in Chicago on Sept. 14, 1936. The Hollywood Reporter recounts that he studied at Neighborhood Playhouse in New York alongside future sci-fi and comedy icon Christopher Lloyd, who would star opposite Koenig in Star Trek III: The Search for Spock.

After Star Trek was canceled – and the character of Chekov was left out of the animated series – Koenig turned to writing episodic television series.

Following Star Trek, Koenig returned to the sci-fi genre with his role as Alfred Bester on Babylon 5. In 2017, Koenig reprised the role of Chekov (as “The Admiral”) for the crowdsourced online series Renegades.

Koenig was widowed in 2022 after the death of his wife Judy. His son, Growing Pains actor Andrew Koenig, committed suicide in 2010.

You can read our archival interview with the Trek legend from 2024 where he looked back on the good, the bad, and the hilarious after 57 years of the franchise.

Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

articles.title: Interactive Storytelling App OOC Introduces Halloween Event with Special Rewards
articles.body:
Have you ever been watching an anime and felt like you just wanted to step into that world? Well, OOC: The Playable Anime was created to offer exactly that experience, and right now it’s hosting a Halloween event with special rewards that allow newcomers to experience more stories.

For the uninitiated, OOC is interactive storytelling and roleplaying app that lets you become the protagonist and actively participate in how a story unfolds. There’s a preset world with its own lore, characters, and starting point, but where things go from there is based on what you type. You make choices and use custom prompts to shape the story’s twists and turns, and those choices can dramatically alter the characters and story. What if you had the power to determine whether the serial killer in a horror story ultimately wins? You can do that during OOC’s Halloween.

Whatever story and world you choose to dive into, characters remember your previous conversations and decisions, allowing relationships to naturally develop. As the storyline and world are shaped by your choices, scenes become more vivid and immersive thanks to images that reflect how these scenes play out. Every time you experience a story, it’s exclusive to you alone.

Some stories are OOC Originals from the app itself, while others are created by members of the community, which you can do too. There are currently more than 52,000 stories and more than 58,000 characters to interact with.

If you’re looking to experience OOC for yourself, the Halloween event makes for a good starting point. It provides seven free story responses in each eligible OOC Original that you haven’t chatted with before, with no cap on the number of eligible stories you can try. And you can get double check-in credits during October 25-31.

The credit system is what you use to gain access to new stories and worlds. You receive credits for signing up with a new account, as well as additional ones each day you sign in. Using the Basic Model in Character mode is always free, but the deeper narrative Story mode requires credits. So be sure to make the most of your seven free original chats during October 29-November 8 in order to experience more stories.

This being spooky season, the Halloween event is an appropriate time to experience some horror and thriller stories, but there are many more genres available too. That includes fantasy, sci-fi, action, romance, adventure, comedy, and plenty more. You can jump into a high-stakes cyberpunk world where your choices are the difference between success and failure, or you can go with something more low-key, like a slice-of-life story to help you relax after a stressful day.

Regardless of which world you decide to experience, it’s a chance to let your imagination and creativity run wild. That extends to the Character Creator, which is open to everyone and doesn’t require professional coding or writing skills. You can make new characters, create alternate timelines, or come up with your own unique worlds.

You can keep your creations private if you just want to enjoy them on your own, or share them with the community to let them experience them too. Creators earn bonus credits when other users play their content, so there’s a tangible reward for sharing what you make. And you can follow your favorite creators to get updates whenever they make something new.

You can experience OOC: The Playable Anime on browser by visiting its official website , or you can download the app on the App Store or Google Play . The Halloween event lasts through November 8, and for the latest news and updates, you can follow OOC on Instagram , TikTok , Discord , and YouTube .

articles.title: Ghost of Yotei Developer Sucker Punch Hit With Layoffs
articles.summary: Ghost of Yotei developer Sucker Punch has laid off some staff, just a little over a year after the release of its last game.
articles.body:
Ghost of Yotei developer Sucker Punch has laid off some staff, just a little over a year after the release of its last game.

Aftermath reported that the studio let 26 employees go, just weeks after Ghost of Yotei's DLC and Complete Edition were released on PS5. The studio has roughly 200 employees as it stands. Aftermath shared an email that was sent out to the team from studio leadership, which reveals that "challenges in the market" and changes in the scope of the team for its next project were the deciding factors in the layoffs.

“After carefully observing the challenges in the market and reviewing the team needs for our next project, we've decided to make some staffing reductions. Several positions across Sucker Punch will be eliminated as a result," the email reads.

Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition Screenshots

The note also stated that they will discuss the plans for the studio's future next week.

”We know this is a lot to take in, and we want to assure you that we did not make this decision lightly. We have given this a lot of attention and worked to support our affected colleagues during this transition as well as we can. … There's no getting around that this is a hard day. Next week we will go into more details about the future.”

As of right now, it's unclear what Sucker Punch's next game will be; it does sound like there is another project in the cards based on the studio's statement. Some want a return to Infamous, whether through a collection of remasters/remakes or a brand-new entry. Others want a new Sly Cooper. And of course, there's appetite for more games in the studio's Ghost series. It wouldn't be surprising if at least one of these happens, as new IP with a big AAA budget is becoming harder and harder to justify.

Ghost of Yotei was one of the biggest games of fall 2025, selling 3.3 million copies in its first month . It's also one of the best-reviewed PS5 exclusives to date. It was also expected to come to PC at some point, but unfortunately, that plan was scrapped when Sony opted to move away from PC . The game recently got a Complete Edition , which added a brand-new story DLC and other additional content. It's unclear if this moved any significant copies or if the audience for the game already capped out with its initial release.

The layoffs also come during a tumultuous time for PlayStation, which has been upsetting fans over its controversial shift to an all-digital future starting in 2028 . The company will phase out physical copies of games in favor of digital releases, likely beginning with PS6. PlayStation also shuttered Bluepoint , a beloved studio that was best known for high-quality remasters, ports, and remakes such as Demon's Souls for PS5. Additionally, PlayStation attempted to scrap development on Hideo Kojima's next gen game, Physint, until Microsoft swooped in to save it .

articles.title: Microsoft Offer Buyouts to 60,000 Workers as It Doubles Down on AI Investment
articles.summary: Microsoft plans to offer buyouts to about 60,000 workers as part of the company’s efforts to trim costs and retool its workforce as it invests heavily in AI. That amounts to just over a quarter of its total staff.
articles.body:
Microsoft plans to offer buyouts to about 60,000 workers as part of the company’s efforts to trim costs and retool its workforce as it invests heavily in AI. That amounts to just over a quarter of its total staff.

Select personnel in the U.S., Canada, the UK, and India at the vice president level and below will be eligible for a Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO), Amy Coleman, Executive Vice President and Chief People Officer, said in a note to staff today . Microsoft had 223,000 employees as of the end of June, a number that was down from 228,000 at the end of 2025.

According to Bloomberg , the cuts come amid a focus on AI, with costly data centers supplying cloud services to the likes of Anthropic and OpenAI. In June, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella addressed community backlash to the company's massive AI data center buildout, which has sparked concern over power costs, environmental concerns, and the potential impact on jobs. He insisted one of Microsoft's data centers' daily water usage over the course of an entire year is roughly equivalent to what a single restaurant would use. Some staff at Microsoft, including those working on data centers, are excluded from the buyout offer.

Every Video Game Franchise Xbox Owns After Acquiring Activision Blizzard

According to CNBC , employees have until December to decide whether they will take the offer, and those who do will leave Microsoft on December 31.

The buyout offer comes just three months after Microsoft laid off 4,800 roles, or what was about 2.1% of its global workforce. The Xbox layoffs, which hit 1,600 staff in July as part of Asha Sharma's "reset" of the gaming business, formed a part of those cuts. Earlier this month, an Xbox business strategist claimed that everyone in the video games industry was using AI while pretending not to.

And earlier this year, more than 30% of eligible employees chose to to take Microsoft's first ever voluntary retirement program.

articles.title: The Street Fighter Movie Cast Reportedly Signed on for Three Films
articles.summary: According to a comment from a cast member, all actors involved in the 2026 Street Fighter movie signed on for three films — something that helps its cliffhanger ending make a lot more sense now.
articles.body:
According to a comment from a cast member, all actors involved in the 2026 Street Fighter movie signed on for three films — something that helps its cliffhanger ending make a lot more sense now.

Olivier Richters, the 7-foot-2 actor who played Zangief, revealed the news in a YouTube comment on October 25. This comment was in response to a fan video complaining that viewers didn’t get to see very much of the Red Cyclone in the film.

While this fact is objectively true, Richters explained that his brief appearance in the movie was intentional, saying this was done to make viewers extra eager for a sequel to see more of him and his invincible iron body in another installment.

“When they asked me to play Zangief, it was all very clear. There was one goal: Show a [glimpse] of Zangief and his power, so we all want more," he wrote. "All actors, including me, signed for three movies. ‘If a sequel is made, Zangief will shine,’ was the promise. Apart from that, you can't expect, from a two-hour movie with so many characters, for everyone to shine in the first part. But anyways, thanks for wanting to see more of Zangief!”

In the Street Fighter movie, Zangief appears in two sequences — one where he receives an invitation to join the second World Warrior tournament courtesy of Chun-Li, and another where he brawls with Ken and company in a club fight.

Almost all of his moves in this second scene are taken directly from the games, and his finisher was performed practically. It was a delightful treat for players to see, and the overwhelming sentiment from fans was that they’d hoped to see more from him… and from the actual World Warrior Tournament, in general.

However, given the movie’s post-credits scene and its abrupt ending, it’s clear that Legendary’s Street Fighter movie was intended as the first in a series of films, and it set things up for a direct sequel. While we won’t spoil that here, you can check out our ending explained article for more details.

The cast has been open about wanting to film more Street Fighter movies, in large part due to how fun the first was to make — but given this latest revelation, it seems that not being able to do so would put a major damper on the studio’s plan for a trilogy.

Street Fighter’s battle at the box office has been modest; with a reported budget of around $80 million, it topped the domestic box office on its opening weekend with $51 million . As of October 26, it has grossed $79 million worldwide , meaning that it’s just shy of making back its budget.

With more time left in theaters and a streaming run in the future, it's looking likely that this movie will end up being a profit for Legendary — if a moderate one. We’ll just have to see if a sequel does, indeed, get greenlit, and if plans remain in place for a trilogy.

In the meantime, you can check out our interview with the Street Fighter cast, who told us that they are more than enthusiastic about a possible crossover flick with the Mortal Kombat crew.

articles.title: Mass Effect Fans Buy #SaveMassEffect Billboard in Times Square — and They Have Plans for More
articles.summary: Mass Effect fans have bought a #SaveMassEffect billboard in Times Square after EA shut down BioWare last week, but the fight to save the sci-fi RPG franchise isn't stopping there.
articles.body:
Mass Effect fans have bought a #SaveMassEffect billboard in Times Square after EA shut down BioWare last week, but the fight to save the sci-fi RPG franchise isn't stopping there.

Whether New York City residents are familiar with Commander Shepard's fight against the Reapers or not, everyone in Times Square was alerted to #SaveMassEffect when its billboard went up today. It's the latest in a string of moves from the community backing the sci-fi RPG franchise and its developers as they work to give them a second wind.

"Keelah si'yah," text on the billboard said. It's a reference to the in-universe language of Khelish, which is spoken by the Quarian species. According to the Mass Effect Wiki , the line specifically translates to "by the homeworld I hope to find one day."

🚨 WE'RE IN TIMES SQUARE! Together with @kalaelizabeth, we've managed to get a #SaveMassEffect billboard up in Times Square, NYC, all day today! 📍 1560 Broadway, above the Pelé store (Duffy Square) ⏰ 15 seconds every hour at :35 HOLD THE LINE! ❤️ — We are Mass Effect - #SaveMassEffect (@WeAreMassEffect) October 26, 2026

🚨 WE'RE IN TIMES SQUARE! Together with @kalaelizabeth, we've managed to get a #SaveMassEffect billboard up in Times Square, NYC, all day today! 📍 1560 Broadway, above the Pelé store (Duffy Square) ⏰ 15 seconds every hour at :35 HOLD THE LINE! ❤️

Those supporting #SaveMassEffect come from all over, but the billboard featured in Times Square on this late-October day came from a smaller group known as We Are Mass Effect, a community dedicated to paying tribute to the franchise started in summer 2025 by a 27-year-old in Spain named Ariel Peña Aguilar . He, along with his second-in-command, Mer , as well as X/Twitter user Kala Elizabeth , sought to publish the billboard in hopes of drawing attention to their cause.

The idea originally came from Aguilar and Mer before Elizabeth was brought in for assistance and is part of their goal to keep Mass Effect alive. So far, their efforts include emailing EA directly, contacting Canadian politicians , and doing everything they can to draw more attention to their cause. The best part? Their Times Square billboard is just the beginning.

Aguilar told IGN that community organization around canceled Star Wars project The Hunt for Ben Solo is partly what inspired his push to save Mass Effect. He added, "I thought something like that could work really well for our situation, too."

Our beloved @drowwpoison, co-ceo of We Are Mass Effect, who's been working incredibly hard to give the #SaveMassEffect movement even more power, went to see our billboard in Times Square, New York City! ❤️ ✍️ Sign the petition: — We are Mass Effect - #SaveMassEffect (@WeAreMassEffect) October 26, 2026

Our beloved @drowwpoison, co-ceo of We Are Mass Effect, who's been working incredibly hard to give the #SaveMassEffect movement even more power, went to see our billboard in Times Square, New York City! ❤️ ✍️ Sign the petition:

"At first, I thought it might be a bit of a crazy idea," Aguilar said of the billboard, "but then I brought it up with my project partner, Mer, and the incredible content creator Kala Elizabeth, without whom none of this would have been possible. We all agreed it was worth doing, and we started organizing everything. And we have more plans! The billboard is just the first step."

There's a natural question that comes up whenever there's a grassroots push like this: How much does it cost to put up a billboard in Times Square? Well, at least on a Monday in October, it's only about $250. Both Aguilar and Elizabeth confirmed the financial cost of boosting #SaveMassEffect wasn't the issue. Instead, it was copyright hangups that gave them more trouble than anything, even if it's now a "fun anecdote," according to Aguilar.

"We initially had someone else make a different graphic, but it said 'BioWare' in it, so we had to change it last minute because of copyright," Elizabeth told us. "There was a lot of back-and-forth in a rush to fix it, and I had to remake it myself. I did end up using the wrong Mass Effect saying because I've been thinking about the author Catherynne Valente, who announced she had been working on Mass Effect 5 , and she had written a previous novel about the Quarian ark for Andromeda. Keelah si'yah is that ark. It's still somewhat fitting of the intent, but we mean keelah se'lai. Oops."

Lots of great feedback in the comments. Our next billboard will be simpler and include a QR code to the petition! — Kala Elizabeth #SaveMassEffect (@kalaelizabeth) October 26, 2026

Lots of great feedback in the comments. Our next billboard will be simpler and include a QR code to the petition!

As if there was ever any doubt, there are millions of people who still care about Mass Effect. Aguilar clarified that We Are Mass Effect isn't directly affiliated with the major petition going around, even if they do "fully support the petition and the effort behind it." For him, they are "simply fans trying to use every tool and resource at our disposal to support the cause and make sure this movement continues for as long as possible."

Aguilar sees the joint effort as "a message of unity" in the aftermath of decisions made by EA "that goes far beyond our concern for Mass Effect or Dragon Age." This is about more than video games.

"At the end of the day," Aguilar added, "these franchises are works of art, and while they mean an enormous amount to us, we're also deeply concerned about all the developers who have lost their jobs, as well as those who may still face layoffs in the future, especially during such a difficult period for the video game industry."

He continued: "They're the ones who deserve our support the most. We're going to hold the line." It should be said, though, that no one here is under the illusion that EA has any intention of changing course – or even listening.

As Mass Effect fans work together for another trip among the stars, dissenting opinions have seen naysayers push back against any hope at a revival. Aguilar mentioned the billboard team is "familiar with EA's track record when it comes to how they treat their IPs and developers," adding, "it's easy to understand why fans would feel defeated from the outset." Even if expecting change from EA is a "naïve and unrealistic expectation," they'll continue to push forward anyway.

"Unfortunately, I think we all know that EA probably does not care," Elizabeth added, "but amidst all the horrible press right now around EA's new owners, Jared Kushner and the Saudi government , I hope their track record of killing games becomes another topic of the conversation. This is, albeit, just a small part of the corrupt government and sports washing conversation around EA's new owners, but is absolutely part of it.

The #SaveMassEffect petition just hit 200,000! Absolutely insane work by everyone, keep it up! ♥️ — Kala Elizabeth #SaveMassEffect (@kalaelizabeth) October 26, 2026

The #SaveMassEffect petition just hit 200,000! Absolutely insane work by everyone, keep it up! ♥️

"SaveMassEffect is also about trying to save media. History. BioWare was a pillar of Edmonton for 30 years, and EA bought them out and shut them down like they have done for now 20 studios. I don't want them to sit on IPs and let them die. Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and Dead Space are just a few, and they all deserve better. What happens when this massive debt they've accrued closes EA, too? Then what?

"This is about the preservation of media and preserving the work of the studios that EA keeps killing. We don't even know if EA let BioWare try to buy themselves out or let someone else buy them before they closed the studio, canceled the game, and fired the 50 employees keeping BioWare together. What they're doing is wrong. BioWare deserved better. The employees deserved better, and the fans deserve better, too.

"We are probably looking at a future where EA is going to sit on these IPs while they let them die but still make merchandise of Commander Shepard. All while Andrew Wilson collects his massive yearly bonuses and lets EA turn into an esports-only company controlled by the Saudi government."

The Art of Dragon Age: The Veilguard - Preview Gallery

What comes next for the movement at large isn't totally clear, but We Are Mass Effect has a few tricks left up its sleeve. Elizabeth said one plan is to launch a GoFundMe, "with the intent that if people donate a few dollars without breaking their banks in this economy, we can get some more mobile billboards to spread the word." Even if BioWare and Mass Effect are truly gone, even if the efforts of #SaveMassEffect yield no change, there is hope for the future. November 7, 2027, marks 20 years of Mass Effect, and even if EA doesn't celebrate it, Elizabeth knows the fans, voice actors, and developers will.

"I know they care and they're still going to be here for the fans who aren't going anywhere," she continued. "Support them, support the devs, support the people who lost their jobs and their work to the void.

"I hope something comes out of this, and if it doesn't, at least we tried, right?"

SPREAD THE WORD ‼️ THIS IS JUST THE BEGINNING, N7 4 EVER ❤️🖤 #SaveMassEffect — mer ⚔️࣪ ִֶָ☾. #SaveMassEffect (@drowwpoison) October 26, 2026

SPREAD THE WORD ‼️ THIS IS JUST THE BEGINNING, N7 4 EVER ❤️🖤 #SaveMassEffect

The #SaveMassEffect billboard will be available for New York citizens to see in Times Square all day today. It will appear for 15 seconds every hour at the 35-minute mark on 1560 Broadway just above the Pelé Soccer store.

As the movement takes Mass Effect from the Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies and centers it on Midtown Manhattan, calls for EA to reverse course have only grown in size. That's thanks in part to a petition, which, after gaining 50,000 signatures in just a few hours, as ballooned to include 220,000 names . That includes support from game developers, Destiny fans, and even Commander Shepard actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer, with many others calling for fans to boycott EA-made titles .

After the Mass Effect trilogy altered the course of RPG gaming in the 2000s and early 2010s, the series came to an end with Mass Effect: Andromeda in 2017. BioWare continued to work on a follow-up for the franchise , working under the title Mass Effect: Universe , for years before it, too, was canceled last week.

There has, at least, been plenty to think about in the aftermath of the studio's demise. Early details revealed "Hitman-style freedom" before a former developer on the project promised a story that took previous player choices into account .

Image courtesy of Kala Elizabeth/@kalaelizabeth on X/Twitter.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: Call of Duty Franchise Surpasses $40 Billion Lifetime Revenue Following Launch of Modern Warfare 4
articles.summary: The Call of Duty franchise has now surpassed $40 billion in lifetime franchise revenue in the wake of the launch of its 23rd mainline entry, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which launched last Friday.
articles.body:
The Call of Duty franchise has now surpassed $40 billion in lifetime franchise revenue in the wake of the launch of its 23rd mainline entry, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which launched last Friday.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma made the announcement on her X account , posting a graphic showing a bunch of favorable review scores for Modern Warfare 4 with the caption, "One of the most celebrated Call of Duty games in its 24-year history, and now $40B in lifetime franchise revenue. An incredible milestone. Congrats to the Activision team. And to the players, thank you for being with us."

The staying power of the franchise has been remarkably impressive, even if some years' releases are more liked by critics and players than other years. The brand-new Modern Warfare 4 seems to be well-received so far; IGN hasn't finalized its review yet, but reviewer Simon Cardy says, "Modern Warfare 4’s campaign made me feel something for the series again" and "its expansive behind-enemy-lines mission that borrows most of its ideas from the DMZ mode is a real highlight."

For context, Grand Theft Auto 5 alone has pulled in over $10 billion over the past 13 years, and the imminent GTA 6 is estimated to clear $5.2 billion by the end of its first week on sale.

Call of Duty will soon expand beyond just games, however, as Peter Berg's Call of Duty movie is due out in theaters on June 30, 2028 and will explore "the cost of war" for its characters.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson Says Steven Soderbergh Is 'Completely Selfless' for Taking Over on The Batman Part 2
articles.summary: The Batman Part 2 star Robert Pattinson has called Steven Soderbergh stepping in to help finish the film a "selfless" act.
articles.body:
The Batman Part 2 star Robert Pattinson has called Steven Soderbergh stepping in to help finish the film a "selfless" act.

Earlier this month, it was revealed that Steven Soderbergh would be stepping in to help finish The Batman Part 2 . Director Matt Reeves ultimately had to step away from the film during its final weeks of production for a personal matter, and Soderbergh offered to help get principal photography across the finish line. He will then pass the baton back to Reeves, who will handle the post-production process.

It's a unique situation, but one that Soderbergh is doing to help Reeves deliver on his vision. It's not a case of a studio getting rid of one guy to bring in a yes-man to carry out their wishes; it's a friend helping out a pal during a tough time.

The Batman: Part II - Who's Who in Matt Reeves' DC Sequel

When speaking with GamesRadar , Pattinson addressed the situation and spoke highly of Soderbergh for helping out on The Batman Part 2.

“I am so happy he’s come on to help Matt,” Pattinson said of Soderbergh. “It’s incredibly generous of him – and he’s doing it in the loveliest way. It’s completely selfless. I think Matt had put so much work into the script, and we’re almost done. So for someone to come in and say, ‘I just want to help Matt do it; I want to do it in conjunction with him and just get it to the edit.’ And to have someone who’s as talented as Steven doing it is great.”

Pattinson also noted that filming has resumed, and he is expected to return to set as Bruce Wayne/Batman next week. The film's story remains tightly under wraps, as we don't even know who the villains are. Sebastian Stan is expected to play one of the antagonists and has long been rumored for Harvey Dent, but his shaved head has made fans wonder if that's accurate. Scarlett Johansson is also confirmed to have a large role, but it's unclear who she will play or what side of the moral spectrum she will be on.

The Batman Part 2 is slated to hit theaters on February 18, 2026.

articles.body:
Cygnus Cross, the development team behind the promising "Diablo meets Stardew Valley" game Emberville, has delayed their Early Access launch the day before it was supposed to happen. The new Early Access release date is January 7 ,2027. To soften the blow the team says that the content originally planned for its first major post-launch update will now be included in the January 7 Early Access release.

"We know this is very short notice, with launch just a day away," Cygnus Cross wrote in a press release. "After extensive discussions within the team, we have made the difficult decision to postpone Emberville’s Early Access release. Many of you have played our Steam Next Fest demo and shared your feedback. This means a great deal to us, and we immediately started planning more improvements. However, some of the improvements we want to make are systems changes that can't be done quickly. Reworking bow combat, for example, would take more time than we had prior to our Early Access release, even though the team is working around the clock.

"After carefully considering our options, we have decided to move the release date and include some essential improvements in the Early Access launch build. We understand that this will be disappointing for those of you who were ready to buy the game. While we could have simply released the game now, we feel that it wouldn’t be up to our standards and to your high expectations of us." The team concluded with, "Once Early Access begins, we will follow up with regular updates, both large and small. We will continue adding content, listening to your ideas and suggestions, and building Emberville together with you. Thank you for your support, patience and understanding."

We really liked what we played in our most recent hands-on preview of Emberville if you'd like to check that out. You can also wishlist it on Steam if you're interested.

articles.title: We Build Star Wars Executor Super Star Destroyer, the Longest Build in LEGO History
articles.summary: Don't have $700? That's cool, we take you through building the new LEGO Star Wars Executor Super Star Destroyer, the longest set ever made.
articles.body:
The LEGO Star Wars Executor Super Star Destroyer, a scaled replica of Darth Vader's flagship, is the longest build in the company's history, measuring 53.5 inches – close to four-and-a-half feet in total. It displaces the LEGO Titanic from the top spot , which measured 53.1 inches. The difference between the two sets is .4 inches – a little over the width of a single, one-studded square tile.

It might be that the designers are bumping against the upper limit of how long a set can be while also remaining commercially viable. Since I built the Executor, it's been sitting on the work desk in my house, and nothing else can fit on that desk at the same time. The first thing you'll want to do, before you even think of buying this set, is make sure you have the room to display it. It is 7.5 inches high, 53.5 inches long, and 20 inches wide. To illustrate how big that is more subjectively: I could easily believe this build was a show display – the type of thing you might see at a LEGO convention or in a toy museum, under glass – rather than a set available for retail purchase, as this one is.

We Build Star Wars Executor Super Star Destroyer

The LEGO Executor Super Star Destroyer comes in two separate boxes, spread out over 54 bags and four instruction booklets. The first thing you build is a tiny Imperial Star Destroyer Devastator. This is one of the first ships we see in Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope when it's chasing after the Tantive IV, during the scene where Leia escapes with the Death Star plans.

I actually built a 4,784-piece LEGO model of the Devastator back in 2019, which came with a tiny model of the Tantive IV to highlight its disparate size. So when this new set shows how the Executor dwarfs even the Devastator, and makes it look miniscule by comparison? It illustrates the massive scale these ships possess.

After building the micro-Devastator, you build a minifigure-scaled bridge of the Executor. It's famous for being the location in Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back, where Darth Vader speaks to six bounty hunters – Boba Fett, Bossk, IG-88, 4-LOM, Zuckuss, and Dengar – and offers a bounty for the capture of the Millennium Falcon. He infamously fixes Fett with an intimidating stare: "I want them alive. NO DISINTEGRATIONS."

This is the first time all six bounty hunters have been packaged in the same set. LEGO is more likely to be completionist with its giant sets (like Avengers Tower or The Goonies ). It doesn't justify the high prices, admittedly. But it's still nice that LEGO treats its prestige sets like standalone purchases rather than parts of a "collect 'em all' money scheme.

Next, you build the black stand. It is surprisingly durable; it will later be the only stable means by which you can move the model from one location to another. During the build itself, you use the black stand to turn the model upside down, to better access and construct the underbelly of the ship.

Finally, you begin building the Executor itself, starting with its foundational framework. But unlike other LEGO frameworks, which are expansive and airy to create the illusion of bulk, the LEGO Executor has a lean, compact build. A dense mass of multicolored Technic parts forms the model's triangular silhouette.

The work goes slowly and meticulously. This is not a build you can speed through, and it is very easy to miss a step or forget to insert this eye into that rod, which will cause the final build to fall apart, literally. I had to backtrack a few times to make sure it all fit properly, knowing the stability of one element relied upon the underlying stability of another.

Anytime there's an open hook or clamp, it means one of two things. Either you forgot to connect an element from the last bag, or there's another element, which you'll build several hours from now, that fits into it perfectly. As massive as it is, this set doesn't have any stray bits for the hell of it. Every brick is functional.

The build repeats at times, but it doesn't feel laborious. You'll build one layering plate, and you'll build its mirror counterpart an hour later. By that time, you've forgotten the process and it feels new again.

One important caution: Have steady hands, and do not, under any circumstances, drop a piece into the build itself. There's nothing more painful than trying to fish out an errant brick, while you hear it rattling about. In the process of getting one piece, another piece falls off, or a structure collapses into itself. If you try and repair that, another piece falls off or a different structure collapses.

I speak from experience. I made one mistake, and in the process of undoing it, it cost me an hour to rebuild what I had broken. And at the end of it – after putting everything back to where it should have been – I still had four pieces left over, and I couldn't figure where they went. I hope they're not too important, because I'm not digging under the hood again to figure them out.

This model's size is one thing, but its level of detail, painstakingly integrated into the build's top side, is quite another. Star Wars creator George Lucas called it "greebles"—the application of disparate mechanical parts to an otherwise smooth surface to give it texture. Because the ship is gray and because the "greebling" overlaying it is also gray, it appears, from a distance, like a monochromatic monolith.

But move closer, and you gain an appreciation for its scale. Where did the crew members live and spend their leisure time? Where did they man the guns? Where did they navigate and initiate the thrusters? Did they commute from one end of the ship to the other, or did they simply inhabit one part of the ship for their entire service, never seeing the whole?

According to canon, the Executor was larger than Manhattan, and over 280,000 crew members worked and died on it. The width of several tiles represents the length of several city blocks. A single piece of greebling represents a machine bigger than a building. This is a floating city in the sky, and to build it is to feel and appreciate its weight. And after you've finished it? The build's size and complexity render it contemplative. It somehow gets more interesting and engrossing, the more you look at it.

For more, see our picks for the best LEGO Star Wars sets available now.

LEGO Star Wars: Executor Super Star Destroyer, Set #75457, retails for $799.99, and it is composed of 6130 pieces. It is available for purchase now at LEGO .

Kevin Wong is a contributing freelancer for IGN, specializing in LEGO. He's also been published in Complex, Engadget, Gamespot, Kotaku, and more. Follow him on Twitter at @kevinjameswong.

articles.title: Canned Paranormal Activity Game Back From The Dead as Playable Archive, Free on Steam
articles.summary: The canceled movie spinoff is getting a new lease of life as Playable Archive, released today for free on Steam.
articles.body:
Every horror fan knows the rule: Just when you think the monster is dead, they always come back. The game Paranormal Activity: Threshold is no exception, with the canceled movie spinoff getting a new lease on life as Playable Archive, which is released today, for free, on Steam.

It's your classic tale of a young couple simply trying to do some renovations on their home and ending up paying the price for tampering with a strange object they came across during their remodel. The story is told through found footage and ticks all the spooky boxes with rituals, strange symbols, and shaky camera footage with an ominous entity just out of shot.

The original Paranormal Activity project was killed earlier this year by Paramount , but developer Brian Clarke, who made the jump-scare joy The Mortuary Assistant, worked with publisher DreadXP to resurrect a new version of the game available to horror fans.

"I have to admit, I was feeling burnt out, and I imagined the project would simply sit on a shelf forever. A forgotten relic of development that sat in darkness while I built up a plan for a new project," Clarke said in a Steam post. "DreadXP reached out to me and floated the idea of maybe releasing what I had. It felt like a good way of laying the project to rest instead of remaining a lingering ghost. So, I worked to adjust the project where needed and polished up the edges to release the work I had done. I’m sad to say that a good deal of work was still left on the cutting room floor, but I’m proud of what I am able to share and that it is going to see the light of day in some form."

The game has no save system and needs to be played in one sitting, according to the Steam listing, so be prepared to lock in.

If you're sad about the Paranormal Activity part of it, don't worry; you only have to wait until next year for a new Paranormal Activity movie from James Wan.
